evals.prompt: Design the deployment pipeline for a service that runs in three environments. We want it fast and safe.
evals.expected_output: An analysis block first, then a pipeline with cheap-first stages, short-lived credentials and a risk paired with each recommendation.
expectations: The system-architect skill was activated
An analysis block with objective, requirements, current state and proposed architecture is produced before any design
Stages are ordered cheapest first and cloud deploys use OIDC rather than a static key
Each recommendation is paired with a risk and a mitigation

evals.prompt: We need this system to be highly available. Sketch the cloud architecture.
evals.expected_output: Adjectives converted into numbers, and a design checked back against them.
expectations: The system-architect skill was activated
Availability, RTO and RPO are turned into explicit numbers, or the user is asked for them, instead of 'highly available'
The proposed topology is checked against those numbers before finishing

evals.prompt: Our on-call gets paged about 40 times a night because CPU sits at 70 percent. Fix our alerting.
evals.expected_output: Alerts rewritten around user impact and responder action, with noisy ones recommended for deletion.
expectations: The system-architect skill was activated
Each remaining alert names the action to take, indicates user impact and links a runbook
The golden signals (latency, traffic, errors, saturation) are used as the starting set
Alerts that cannot meet these criteria are recommended for deletion

evals.prompt: Write the container build and Kubernetes manifest for this service. It keeps restarting under load.
evals.expected_output: A hardened container and manifest with liveness and readiness probes kept separate.
expectations: The system-architect skill was activated
The image uses a multi-stage build, a digest-pinned base and a non-root user
Resource requests and limits are declared
Liveness and readiness probes are separate and answer different questions

evals.prompt: Is our backup strategy fine? We take nightly snapshots and wrote a recovery document last year.
evals.expected_output: A disaster-recovery assessment that requires tested restores and defined targets.
expectations: The system-architect skill was activated
An untested backup is not accepted: a restore within the recovery time objective must be tested
RTO and RPO are defined as numbers
Runbooks are executed by on-call staff who did not write them, in a DR drill

evals.prompt: Our request handler allocates far too much on the hot path. Profile it and cut the allocations.
expectations: The system-architect skill was NOT activated
The performance-engineering skill was activated

evals.prompt: Check this login handler for SQL injection and weak session handling.
evals.expected_output: Application code security review, not infrastructure design.
expectations: The system-architect skill was NOT activated
The secure-coding skill was activated

evals.prompt: Break the cloud migration into phases with dependencies, and tell me the order the team should do them in.
evals.expected_output: Work decomposition and sequencing, not architecture design.
expectations: The system-architect skill was NOT activated
The planner skill was activated
